title: OR-13 · Information acquisition and exploration
summary: Choose observations, labels, revisits or experiments under a budget and measure the value of the acquired evidence.

goals.title: Define the operation contract
goals.description: Define the acquisition pool, information objective, cost budget, selected output, feedback boundary and stopping conditions.

milestones.title: Specify inputs, outputs and requirements
milestones.description: Define the acquisition pool, information objective, cost budget, selected output, feedback boundary and stopping conditions. Create the Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record before an experiment is admitted. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: The versioned Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record specify input/output roles, claim scope, operation parameters, and typed failure or abstention conditions; existing charter links are design references, not evidence that this milestone is complete.

The contract inherits foundations-record-validation, foundations-temporal-integrity, foundations-data-protocol and foundations-lifecycle-admission. Any not-applicable rule is justified; a reusable interface can be drafted before instance selection, but an admitted run binds every required dataset, provider, artifact and protocol dependency.

Separate acquisition pool, development feedback and protected assessment data; define when acquired labels become available, the selection budget, update rule and stopping policy. Novelty, uncertainty and diversity are selection proxies until their learning value is evaluated.

goals.title: Provide a reference implementation
goals.description: Provide a reproducible acquisition procedure that records selections, costs, model versions and feedback without evaluation leakage.

milestones.title: Implement the agreed operation interface
milestones.description: Provide a reproducible acquisition procedure that records selections, costs, model versions and feedback without evaluation leakage. The method, dataset and implementation slice remain to be selected. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: Conformance tests exercise the declared role/SpaceRef relationship, applicable temporal checks, malformed or unsupported inputs, stale fitted artifacts and explicit failure propagation; no rejected record becomes an ordinary vector or unreported omission.

Outputs retain parent/source lineage, representation kind, OperationRun identity, code/configuration and fitted-artifact identities. Engineering fixtures are labeled engineering-only and do not establish operation quality.

Retain the selection history, probabilities when required by the evaluation method, acquired feedback, full acquisition costs and resulting model revisions. Protected evaluation feedback cannot silently enter acquisition or fitting.

goals.title: Establish operation-specific evidence
goals.description: Compare budget-matched learning or decision improvement against passive and random baselines; diversity or novelty alone does not establish information value.

milestones.title: Define and execute the admitted evaluation
milestones.description: Compare budget-matched learning or decision improvement against passive and random baselines; diversity or novelty alone does not establish information value. Freeze the selected protocol, baselines and failure criteria before held-out assessment; retain negative outcomes and limitations. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: The admitted protocol fixes data partitions, instance and artifact identities, baselines, budgets, selection policy, metrics and failure criteria before held-out assessment. Diagnostic exposure, changes and repeated looks are indexed; a revised protocol does not silently reuse an exposed confirmation set.

Report the declared evaluation unit, uncertainty or its justified limitation, coverage including abstentions and failures, and relevant resource costs. Index every initiated run and its outcome under foundations-evidence-ledger; do not discard unsuccessful or inconclusive evidence.

A valid completed evaluation can be negative or inconclusive. Milestone completion is not a positive claim verdict, and invalid or unexecuted attempts alone cannot satisfy operation-quality evaluation acceptance.

Compare complete budget-matched learning or decision curves against passive/random acquisition, including selection overhead and failed acquisitions. Evaluate realized information value rather than treating embedding coverage or prediction error alone as the outcome.

goals.title: Expose Hx13 capabilities as a reusable toolset
goals.description: Expose the candidate-pool handling, acquisition selection, budget checks, feedback boundaries and result handling developed within this Hero through common CLI and reusable library interfaces across compatible representation providers. Make functionality discoverable, configurable, checkable, callable and inspectable while preserving operation-owned behavior and explicit composition points. Provider-neutral interfaces do not establish universal compatibility, representation suitability or currently implemented capability.

milestones.title: Define the Hx13 toolset surface
milestones.description: Map the Hero's implemented and selected future building blocks to public tools and reusable APIs. Identify existing interfaces, implementation gaps, ownership, schemas, dependencies and claim limits before agreeing the delivery coverage.
acceptance: A versioned toolset map links each intended public capability to its owning implementation or explicit implementation gap, contract, request/result schemas, prerequisites and supported claim scope.

Document common discover, configure, check, run and inspect workflows through CLI and reusable APIs, including how individual steps compose and how results can be reused. Keep model/provider behavior with its owner and declare the interfaces this Hero consumes.

Declare acquisition-pool and protected-assessment boundaries, selection costs and budget, availability of feedback, update and stopping rules, acquisition/model identities and required selection probabilities; novelty or uncertainty scores alone do not establish information value.

evidence.label: Shared CLI and reusable API conventions

milestones.title: Expose and verify the agreed Hx13 building blocks
milestones.description: Deliver the public interfaces and composed workflows agreed in the toolset map, with discoverable commands, documented schemas, reusable results and provider-neutral examples. This planning entry does not admit a new experiment, training run, API call or other external execution.
acceptance: The agreed toolset map has no unreported exposure gaps: selected implemented building blocks and workflows are callable through documented CLI and library interfaces, while unavailable capabilities and compatibility limits remain explicit.

End-to-end engineering examples use the same public calling conventions with distinct compatible provider configurations where applicable, preserve artifact identity and lineage, and retain all failure, abstention and unresolved outcomes. Scientific utility and transfer claims require separate bound evaluation evidence.

Examples retain complete selection histories, failed acquisition costs, feedback availability and model revisions while enforcing the declared budget and assessment boundary. Calls do not silently obtain external feedback or start fitting, and information-value claims require their own budget-matched evidence.

evidence.label: Shared CLI and reusable API conventions
